To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incorporation of GO and reactive clay nanofillers into the PVA/ODAsalt matrix-partner polymer blends can lead to the fabrication of nanofiber membranes with unique surface morphological features and good conductivity, which can also be used as semi-conductive, bioactive platforms in the immobilization of biomolecules.

the incorporation of GO nanosheets with reactive organoclay in PVA-based nanofibers leads to the formation of unique nanofibrous structures with good conductivity, which can be used as semi-conductive matrices in bioengineering processes.
the electrospinning technique was successfully used to prepare nanofibers from PVA/ODAmMT/PMO/GO nanocomposites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication and characterization of new polymer nanofibrous materials with potential applications in electrochemical devices and biomedical engineering.
the fabrication and characterization of a novel nanofiber electrolyte with good conductivity and biocompatibility.
the design, synthesis, and characterization of novel nanocomposite and nanofiber electrolyte materials for potential use in bioengineering and biomedical fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study is the first report on the fabrication, characterization, and biological response of the novel nanocomposite nanofibers for potential applications in bioengineering and electrochemical processes.
the incorporation of reactive organoclay and GO as reinforcement fillers in the PVA/ODAsolution blends leads to the formation of PVA/GO-ODA-MMT reactive polymer nanocomposite nanofibers.

the intercalated nanocomposites and electrospun nanofibrous mats with unique morphological features, high surface-to-volume ratio and high electrical conductivity can be successfully prepared from PVA/ODAMMT nanocomposite and poly (maleic anhydride-alt-1-octaldecene)-g-Graphene oxide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrospun nanofibers can be used as a promising platform for bone tissue engineering applications.

we have demonstrated a new approach for fabrication of novel polymer nanocomposite and nanofibrous structures with improved mechanical, electric and thermal properties, which are suitable for various applications in tissue engineering, biosensors and biomedical devices.

the incorporation of reactive organoclay into the polymer solution and its subsequent exfoliation in the nanofibers is a promising strategy for the fabrication of novel polymer nanocomposites and electroactive nanofibrous scaffolds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nanofibrous structure and the surface morphology of the fabricated nanofibers can be controlled by the choice of the matrix-partner solution blends and the addition of GO and reactive organoclays.

the interfacial interaction and chemical structure of nanocomposites play a crucial role in the fabrication of nanofibrous structures with unique surface morphological characteristics and good conductivity.
the incorporation of GO and ODA-MMT into the PVA/MA-1-octene copolymer nanofiber matrix is an effective approach for improving their thermal stability, conductivity and biocompatibility.
